item.title: Applications open for 2027 Correctional Officer Training Program
item.description:
Applications open for 2027 Correctional Officer Training Program jenniferdhogan Tue, 10/27/2026 - 10:19

The provincial government, in partnership with the Atlantic Police Academy is continuing to help Island residents pursue a career in correctional services at a reduced cost.

The Correctional Officer Training Program helps prepare students for a career in corrections and ensures there are enough qualified officers to staff correctional facilities. 

“The Correctional Officer Training Program sets students up for success in a career in public safety. Graduates are eligible for an interview to be a casual correctional officer in PEI, and they can apply for permanent positions after one year. This helps make sure our corrections system is well-staffed with qualified people.”

- Minister of Justice and Public Safety Bloyce Thompson

The next cohort will begin on January 4, 2027. This six-month program consists of 17 weeks of coursework followed by a seven-week on-the-job training placement at correctional centres across the Island. Graduates of the program will receive a correctional officer diploma from the Atlantic Police Academy.

Individuals accepted into the program may be eligible for a range of supports, including a substantial tuition reduction. Participants may also receive assistance from Skills PEI to help cover costs such as mileage and childcare. Those who are unemployed or underemployed and meet eligibility criteria may qualify for Employment Insurance.

"Building a skilled workforce means creating opportunities for Islanders to pursue meaningful careers in every sector, including public safety," said Minister of Workforce and Advanced Learning Jenn Redmond. "Through SkillsPEI, we are helping individuals access the training and supports they need to succeed in the Correctional Officer Training Program while contributing to safer, stronger communities across Prince Edward Island."

The deadline to apply is November 13, 2026 at noon. 

For eligibility and application requirements, visit Correctional Officer Training Program.

item.description:
Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems for Pesticide Application slmacneil Mon, 10/26/2026 - 15:15
Publication type: Guidelines

A Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (RPAS) consists of a navigable aircraft (otherwise known as a drone) operated by a pilot who is not on board plus all system elements that are required for flight operations. Health Canada and the PEI Department of Land and Environment have approved RPAS (ie. drones) for use to apply pesticides that are registered for RPAS and aerial use.

item.title: MyPEI Account In-person Verification - O’Leary Public Library
item.description:
MyPEI Account In-person Verification - O’Leary Public Library tlpeters Mon, 10/26/2026 - 14:17

Drop by a participating public library during Digital Health Week and let us help you verify your MyPEI Account and get connected to MyHealthPEI.

With MyHealthPEI, you can:

  • View recent lab results and imaging reports
  • See your vaccination records
  • Track some of your health information online

A verified MyPEI Account gives you access to MyHealthPEI and other provincial online government services. Visit us in-person (no appointment needed) and we'll help you get set up!

To verify your account in-person, you’ll need two pieces of valid ID

  • Primary ID: Must be one of the following:
    • PEI Driver’s License
    • Voluntary ID
  • Secondary ID: Choose one from the following list:
    • Birth Certificate
    • Canadian Citizenship Card
    • Permanent Resident Card
    • Certificate of Indian Status
    • Canadian Passport
    • Nexus Card
    • Official Immigration Document

You will also need:

  • To be at least 16 years of age
  • A mobile phone, tablet, or laptop
  • Access to your email

Bring along your PEI Health Card if you would like help linking your health information to your account.

November 20, 2026 1:00 pm to November 20, 2026 3:00 pm

O'Leary Public Library
18 Community Street
O'Leary PE C0B 1V0
Canada

item.title: PEI property tax payment reminder
item.description:
PEI property tax payment reminder jenniferdhogan Mon, 10/26/2026 - 14:11

Property owners across the Island are reminded that the final instalment of their 2026 property taxes is due Nov. 30, 2026.

Property tax payments can be made in one of the following ways:

  • By cash, cheque or debit at any Access PEI site.
  • By cash, cheque or debit at a financial institution. Automatic payments are encouraged to avoid interest charges.
  • By cheque using the provincial drop box located at 95 Rochford St., First Floor, Shaw Building South, Charlottetown.
  • By mailing a cheque to:
    Province of Prince Edward Island
    Finance and Affordability
    P.O. Box 880
    Charlottetown, PE
    C1A 7M2

PEI property tax statements were mailed to all property owners in May 2026. Replacement copies can be requested online or property owners can use the property tax balance inquiry to check their outstanding balances.

Anyone with questions or who needs assistance with their property taxes can email taxandland@gov.pe.ca or call 902-368-4070.

Learn more about PEI property taxes here.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
Ph: 867-767-9140 ext. 11092
